findings.text: The virtual CPU run exit payload includes a system event member holding type plus count plus either flags or sixteen data words, a register access member holding user error plus padding plus kernel reason plus index plus bidirectional value, a notification member holding flags, a memory fault member holding flags plus guest address plus length, and a confidential compute member holding flags plus number plus choice among unknown plus quote plus vmcall information plus event setup variants each starting with return and then carrying variant addresses sizes leaves or vectors with unknown carrying five data words and quote carrying address with size and vmcall carrying leaf with four registers and notify carrying vector.

The same payload also offers secure channel data with address plus register plus reserved plus function plus two selectors of differing widths, single byte interrupt vector, opaque hypervisor plus xen plus certificate nests, ARM fault pairing syndrome with fault address, RISC-V call plus register records using native words for identifiers arguments returns values and masks, ARM error with flags plus syndrome plus virtual plus guest addresses, fixed 256 byte tail reserving union capacity, and footer with valid plus dirty 64 bit masks plus architecture defined synchronized block padded to 2048 bytes.

Run area numbers are KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_CRASH uses 3 plus KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_WAKEUP uses 4 plus KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_SUSPEND uses 5 plus KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_SEV_TERM uses 6 plus KVM_SYSTEM_EVENT_TDX_FATAL uses 7, KVM_MSR_EXIT_REASON_INVAL uses bit 0 plus KVM_MSR_EXIT_REASON_UNKNOWN uses bit 1 plus KVM_MSR_EXIT_REASON_FILTER uses bit 2 with KVM_MSR_EXIT_REASON_VALID_MASK covering those three, KVM_NOTIFY_CONTEXT_INVALID uses bit 0, KVM_MEMORY_EXIT_FLAG_PRIVATE uses bit 3 of 64 bits, KVM_EXIT_ARM_SEA_FLAG_GPA_VALID uses bit 0 of 64 bits, SYNC_REGS_SIZE_BYTES uses 2048, and exit tail pad uses 256.

Deferred input output description has a zone record holding 64 bit base plus 32 bit extent plus selector between pad and port flag, a transaction record holding 64 bit guest address plus 32 bit length plus same pad or port selector plus eight data bytes, and a ring header holding consumer plus producer positions followed by flexible trailing transaction array whose capacity equals page size minus header size divided by transaction size.

Small control records are translation taking 64 bit linear input and returning 64 bit physical output plus valid plus writable plus user mode flags, interrupt taking 32 bit number, dirty tracking taking slot plus padding plus either user bitmap pointer or 64 bit pad where clear variant adds page count plus first page, signal mask holding length plus flexible bytes, task priority control holding enable plus flags plus eight reserved words, and virtual APIC address holding 64 bit value.

Size plus direction rules are single bitmap bit corresponds to each guest page in dirty tracking, ioeventfd length zero skips length comparison while other lengths match exact widths, coalesced ring first plus last delimit queued entries, sync masks separate host supplied valid classes from user dirtied classes, msr error flows user to kernel while reason plus index flow kernel to user with data bidirectional, and some capability queries return counts not booleans.

Fragile aspects are user bitmap pointers dereferenced by kernel, flexible trailing arrays needing length checks, architecture defined sync plus debug blocks varying by build, overlapping pad versus port selectors, and exact numeric ioctl plus capability codes where numeric gaps exist.
